name: Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF)

doctrine.summary: The Kurdish-led, multi-ethnic force of north-east Syria, built around the YPG and the women's YPJ with Arab, Syriac and other components. From 2015 it was the US-led coalition's main ground partner against the Islamic State, took Raqqa (2017) and Baghouz (2019), and guarded tens of thousands of IS detainees and the al-Hol and Roj camps. After Assad's fall it fought Turkish-backed Syrian National Army factions (Tishrin Dam, early 2025), signed an integration agreement with Damascus in March 2025, and after a January 2026 government offensive accepted a 29 January 2026 ceasefire that handed Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor to the government and began folding the SDF into Syrian army brigades. By mid-2026 four SDF brigades had been formed (two in Kobani and Hasakah) and about 6,000 members registered on army payrolls, while Qamishli, Hasakah and Kobani remained under SDF/Kurdish administration and a former YPG commander became a deputy defence minister. IS detention sites were handed over in 2026. The force is light infantry with good small-unit skills, snipers and drone use, US-supplied vehicles and many local up-armoured trucks.
doctrine.fireteam: Tabur (company) sections of 8-10 in pickups or Humvees; mixed-sex YPJ units; battle-buddy pairs with strong sniper support.
tactics: Counter-IS raids and sweeps in the Euphrates valley and desert, often with partner special forces
Defence of towns with prepared positions, tunnels and sniper nests
Snipers and anti-materiel rifles as the backbone of defensive fights
Commercial and FPV drones for surveillance and strikes
Guarding detention sites and camps (prison-break defence)

camo.name: Khaki / olive field uniform
camo.use: Most YPG/YPJ and SDF units; coloured scarves

grenadier: AK with GP-25 / M4 with M203
squad_leader: M4 carbine with optic or AKM
sniper: Locally made 12.7 mm / 14.5 mm anti-materiel rifles

body_armor.notes: Line units: chest rigs, some soft vests (light). Counter-terror units (YAT): US-supplied helmets and plate carriers (medium).

vehicles.notes: Pickups with DShK and PKM, often with welded side plates.
US-supplied Humvees (M1151 etc.) of YAT and commando units.
Unarmed pickups and up-armoured local trucks.
MRAPs supplied to counter-IS partners, used at detention sites and on raids.
ZU-23-2 on pickups and trucks for fire support.
Commercial and FPV drones used in the 2025 Tishrin Dam fighting and against IS cells.
A few captured T-55s and old armour (game rarity).

support_assets: ZU-23 and DShK fire support on trucks
Historically coalition air support (US forces left Syria in early 2026)

as_client: Counter-IS raid on a desert cell or weapons cache
Reinforce a detention site or camp against a breakout attempt
Escort aid convoys to camps (al-Hol type)
Recover kidnapped staff or local officials
Train and accompany a counter-terror unit

notes: Situation as of October 2026: integration into the Syrian state is under way but incomplete. The January 2026 government offensive and the 29 January ceasefire moved Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor under Damascus; SDF brigades are being formed inside the army; Kurdish-majority Qamishli, Hasakah and Kobani are still SDF/Autonomous Administration-run; IS detention sites were handed over in 2026 and IS attacks have risen in Raqqa and Deir ez-Zor. US forces left Syria in February-March 2026. syr -> sdf is -20 and sdf -> syr is -15 (tense partners in an unfinished integration, not open war). Türkiye regards the SDF as linked to the PKK (which announced dissolution in 2025) and remains hostile. Game: an early-game client for counter-IS work in levant_syria and mesopotamia (Syria-Iraq border). Proposal: if integration completes during the campaign, the SDF could fold into syr as a sub-faction.
proposed: folding sdf into syr if integration completes (campaign event)
